newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chechens seek leader in ruins of war.
newsitem.headline: Chechens seek leader in ruins of war.

text.p: Russia's rebel Chechen region voted on Monday amidst the ruins of a two-year war for a president to press ahead with the struggle for independence from Moscow and foreign recognition.

In some places, guerrillas in camouflage uniform stacked kalashnikovs in the corner before entering polling booths, but good-humoured crowds were dominated by civilians, women in headscarves, men in fur and traditional sheepskin hats.

"We need an end to chaos and these elections will put us on the road to a better life," said Musa Sagalayev, 45, after casting his ballot in Grozny, in sight of the towering, snow-capped Caucasus mountains.

In Moscow, Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, opposed to any move to sovereignty, said he was unconcerned by anti-Russian rhetoric in the campaign. "Let the elections take place, let everything cool down and then we'll sit at a table and work together," he told journalists.

Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov, whose forces suffered humiliating defeats here before withdrawal this month, said a special command centre was being set up to secure the border between Chechnya and the Russian hinterland.

Turnout was so great among an electorate estimated at around half a million that officials ordered polling stations to stay open for an extra two hours until 10 p.m. (1900 GMT). First results could come by late on Monday night.

All the main contenders in the 13-man field vow to turn the de facto independence won in the war into sovereignty. They include acting president Zelimkhan Yandarbiyev and guerrilla leader Salman Basayev, who is wanted in Russia for "terrorism".
Aslan Maskhadov, 45, who led the Chechen guerrilla fighters to a stunning victory over the Russian army last August, headed straw polls last week.
A vote in excess of 50 percent would secure victory in the first round. If no candidate garners more than half the vote there will be a two-man runoff in two weeks.

President Boris Yeltsin, who has admitted that sending troops to crush Chechen secession in 1994 was a mistake, agreed to elections as part of a face-saving peace deal. The issue of sovereignty was deferred for five years but leading candidates insist they would, if elected, press the matter with Moscow.
The Kremlin would prefer Maskhadov and abhors Basayev but, in any case, flatly opposes independence for fear of unsettling its southern frontier and fuelling other ethnic conflicts.

Patient queues built up at polling stations early on a bright winter morning, from snow-clad villages in the Caucasus mountains to Soviet-era collective farms on the plain, in the deavastated capital Grozny and at special centres where busloads of war refugees poured in from across the frontier.

At Basayev's mountain stronghold of Vedeno, a centre of resistance throughout the war, one hobbling village elder in a shaggy sheepskin hat entered the polling station with the Moslem warcry "Allahu Akbar!" (God is Greatest).
The wail was taken up by dozens of others on a street still scarred by the ruins of homes hit by Russian shells. Islam has inspired rejection of Russian rule for two centuries.

More than 100 foreign observers are in Chechnya to monitor an election for the first time. Several observers from the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) said they were impressed by the smoothness of the process.

Casting his ballot at a old dairy collective farm 20 km (12 miles) northwest of Grozny, Maskhadov predicted he would win 60 percent of the vote. He pledged to "bring order" to Chechnya as his first step and to develop normal ties with Russia.
"We need to develop normal ties so that we won't have to wage war any more," said the grey-haired former Soviet artillery colonel, dressed in a traditional lambswool hat.

Basayev, 32, who made his name with a bloody raid on the southern Russian town of Budennovsk in 1995, insisted he would win and warned Russia it would "collapse" if it failed to accept Chechen independence.
